inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped event report computes many distinct actor and event counts under different FILTER predicates in one projection, separating broad activity from event-specific contributor and event totals.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a project event matrix. Fixed projects are left joined to events, PostgreSQL COUNT(DISTINCT ...) FILTER predicates become COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END), and several actor- and event-level categories are computed together while an eventless project remains visible. The source dates, schema, names, event corpus, and dashboard context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Project 11 has repeated actors across push, issue, review, and comment events; project 22 has one issue; project 33 has no events and must remain with zero conditional counts.
determinism_notes: Project IDs, event IDs, actor IDs, event kinds, CASE predicates, grouping, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE project_catalog (project_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE project_events (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_id INT NOT NULL, actor_id INT NOT NULL, event_kind VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_code, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_kind IN ('issue', 'push', 'review') THEN e.actor_id END) AS active_contributors, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_kind = 'push' THEN e.actor_id END) AS pushers, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_kind = 'review' THEN e.actor_id END) AS reviewers, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_kind = 'issue' THEN e.event_id END) AS issue_events, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.event_kind IN ('comment', 'review') THEN e.event_id END) AS discussion_events FROM project_catalog AS p LEFT JOIN project_events AS e ON e.project_id = p.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_code ORDER BY p.project_id
